title: The haves and the have-nots
subtitle: poverty line, deprived, affluent, make ends meet
summary: Write and speak precisely about wealth and poverty - absolute and relative poverty, deprivation and destitution, affluence - and use the everyday idioms for having too little money.

lesson.heading: Defining poverty
lesson.text: The United Nations says that **fundamentally** - in a basic and important way - poverty is a **denial** of choices and opportunities, a **violation** of human **dignity**. To deny people something is not to allow them to have it; a violation is an act that spoils or destroys something.

examples.text: **Denial** of people's basic human freedoms is wrong.
Poverty could be said to be a **violation** of human **dignity**.
**Fundamentally**, poverty is a denial of choices and opportunities.

lesson.heading: Types of poverty
rows: being poor according to a fixed minimum standard, sometimes called the poverty line
being poor in relation to others around you; it depends on a person's social context
living below the poverty line; another word for this is penury
being poor in a range of ways, not only financial
lesson.note: Relative poverty takes into account that there is no income equality between countries.

lesson.heading: The social factors
lesson.text: Human poverty takes into account **shelter** (having a place to live protected from the weather), **nutrition** - people living in poverty are more likely to be **malnourished** - **literacy** levels, since they are more likely to be **illiterate**, **sanitation**, and access to education and healthcare. People lacking these basic things are said to be **deprived**.

examples.text: Food and **shelter** are two of the most important human needs.
Children who don't get enough food suffer ill health as a result of **malnourishment**.
Inadequate **sanitation** can have serious health consequences.
The number of children facing **deprivation** is increasing.

lesson.note: Sanitation is the system for taking dirty water and waste away from homes to ensure good hygiene.

lesson.heading: Wealth and poverty

left.label: Wealth
examples: Only a small minority of people in the world enjoy **affluence**.
Our family enjoyed a relatively **affluent** lifestyle at that time.
The **super-rich** control much of the world's wealth.

right.label: Poverty
examples: His family were once quite affluent, but they have become increasingly **impoverished**.
Many people left the **poverty-stricken** countryside to go to the city.
Everywhere you see **destitute** people living in shop doorways.

lesson.note: Destitute people have no money, food, home or possessions; the noun is destitution.

lesson.heading: Living on very little
lesson.text: People **on or below the breadline** have the income of an extremely poor person. When your income is low it is hard to **make ends meet** - to have enough money for all you need - and you may be **living from hand to mouth**, with just enough money to live without suffering.

examples.text: Over 60% of the population live on or below the **breadline**.
It can be hard for students to **make ends meet**.
When we were first married, we were **living from hand to mouth**.

lesson.heading: When money is short
lesson.text: If **money is tight**, there is not much of it. To **tighten your belt** is to spend less than before. An **income bracket** is a range of income with an upper and a lower level, and people can be **classed as** - categorised as - poor.

examples.text: Ever since I lost my job, money has been **tight**.
If we all **tighten our belts**, we should be able to manage all right.
Many of the people in this area are in the lowest **income bracket**.
Many of the children here are **classed as** living in poverty.

lesson.text: We say the rich and the poor, meaning rich people and poor people - never ~~the riches and the poors~~.

exercises.prompt: Match each type or aspect of poverty with its definition.

pairs.right: being poor according to a fixed minimum standard
being poor in relation to others around you
being poor in a range of ways, not only financial
having no money, food, home or possessions at all

exercises.prompt: Millions of people still live below the poverty ___.
exercises.explanation: The poverty line is the fixed minimum standard used to define absolute poverty.

exercises.prompt: Food and ___ are two of the most important human needs.
exercises.hint: (a place to live protected from the weather)
exercises.explanation: Shelter is having somewhere to live that is protected from the weather.

exercises.prompt: Most of the people who live in this street are in a higher income ___.
exercises.explanation: An income bracket is a range of income with upper and lower levels.

exercises.prompt: It can be hard for students to make ___ meet.
exercises.hint: (have enough money for all you need)
exercises.explanation: To make ends meet is to have enough money to buy everything you need.

exercises.prompt: If we all tighten our ___, we should be able to manage all right.
exercises.explanation: To tighten your belt is to spend less money than before.

exercises.prompt: I was surprised how poverty-___ the villages looked given the richness of the surrounding farmland.
exercises.explanation: Poverty-stricken means badly affected by poverty.

exercises.prompt: There are far fewer ___ people in the world than there used to be, so literacy levels are rising.
exercises.explanation: Literacy is the ability to read and write; the opposite condition is being illiterate.

exercises.prompt: It is not very meaningful to talk in terms of ___ poverty when you compare people who live in very different contexts.
exercises.explanation: Absolute poverty uses a fixed minimum standard; relative poverty compares people with those around them.

exercises.prompt: A person who sleeps in a cardboard box on the street and begs for money can best be described as ___.
exercises.explanation: Destitute is the strongest word: without money, food, home or possessions.

exercises.prompt: Even children with rich parents can be ___ in terms of love and affection.
exercises.explanation: Deprived means lacking things considered necessary for a pleasant life, not only money.

exercises.prompt: The country has great extremes of poverty and ___.
exercises.explanation: Affluence means wealth; do not confuse it with influence.

exercises.statement: Without my husband's income, we were very much living from hand to foot.
exercises.explanation: The idiom is living from hand to mouth - having just enough money to live without suffering.

exercises.statement: Someone who is in penury is living in extreme poverty.
exercises.explanation: Correct - penury is another word for extreme poverty.

exercises.prompt: Does each expression describe having plenty, or having very little?

exercises.answer: Relative poverty is being poor in relation to others around you
exercises.explanation: Relative poverty depends on a person's social context.
